title: A small kitchen project and a larger comparison
intro: Build a small-kitchen package and compare medium/large cases, identifying reusable details and changes that require renewed review.

sections.title: Assemble the small-kitchen package
sections.text: Combine user brief, site survey, layout, elevations, sections, devices, services and hardware. Test openings and reconcile cut lists to drawing revisions. List open issues before release; limited area does not remove access or service needs.
sections.caption: A small project still needs every coordination interface.

sections.title: Compare what changes with scale
sections.text: Larger cases may introduce zones, users, appliances or an island. For each difference record its cause, affected elements, drawings/services and owner. Reuse a detail only if its conditions remain valid; floor-area growth does not scale drawer dimensions or fixing capacity.
sections.caption: Compare changed use, not just floor-area ratios.

sections.title: Reconcile quantities and approvals separately
sections.text: Quantity exercise: 4 base and 3 wall units total 7. The larger case has ⁦6 + 4 + 1 = 11⁩ base/wall/tall units, 4 more cabinets. This does not state panel count or cost difference. Each case needs its own part, service and inspection records.
sections.caption: 7 and 11 count cabinets, not panels or prices.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The larger option adds an island. Updating cabinet counts alone misses changed movement, services and support. Create a difference card instead of copying the small-project approval.
example.decision: Decision: review changed execution conditions before reusing the package.

quiz.question: How many cabinets are 6 base, 4 wall and 1 tall?
quiz.explanation: The three counts total 11 cabinets, not panels.

assignment.prompt: Submit a small-kitchen package, medium/large difference cards, cabinet counts and reopened review items.

faq.question: Can details scale by the room-area ratio?
faq.answer: No. Parts, products, support and services need condition-specific review.
